The other competitors, however, were over half a mile ahead and consisted of Kilby (Coventry)Bullivant(Derby) Tim Johnston (Portsmouth) and Price (Bristol) - hardly the four that Bill would have selected to have given such a start over a 6 mile leg.
Geoff split the Coventry team most convincingly,beating Kilby,Taylor and Heatley,but had to give best to Adcocks (an easy winner) and Horne who beat Geoff in the run in.

After one lap he was still in the twenties and although he began to make ground on the second circuit it was a slow and painful business against such opposition as Adcocks and Kilby (Coventry), Rose, Wheeler and Wyatt (New Zealand), Tulloh, Roberts and Barlow.
Could Bill Kerr keep close enough to Kilby and Bullivant to give our last three runners a chance or would these top class runners open up a large gap?
…bout 30 seconds behind the leaders who were North Staffs (Shelley), Portsmouth (Lindsell), Bristol (Edwards), Coventry (Kilby), Bournemouth (Stewart) and Ilford (Batchelor) in that order.…
At this point Coventry, through a stage record run by Kilby, were almost a minute clear of the second team and 4 minutes and 20 seconds ahead of Belgrave.

Dick Taylor, their fast improving 5,000 metres runner will be a useful pacemaker for those marathon medallists Adcocks and Kilby. In addition,there is every chance that their cross country internationals Juan Taylor (only once outside the'teens in the last four Nationals) and John Hammond will be well to the fore.
With Heatley and Kilby both in form again and Bartlett and Lancaster to join their winning 'National' team (9 in 117) they should be a stronger force than last year's winning dozen.

The arrival at Godiva of Colin Kirkham and the revival of Kilby and Heatley were too much for the opposition, and although our team ran well it was evident early on that it was all in an effort to get second place.
Since previous fast times on this course have been run by Kilby, Juan & Dick Taylor, Adcocks and Tim Johnston, this run of Gerry's is indicative of his present excellent form.

Geoff North returning to the team for the first time after his wedding fought hard to get with the leaders but Rhodes of Derby and Kilby of Coventry proved to be better and we dropped back to a deficit of 1 min. 44 secs although staying in third place.

Bill's best London to Brighton run was in the National event of April 1962 when he recorded 6th fastest time on the long stage 9 with only Kilby, Bullivant, Craig, Freary and Tulloh (all internationals) being faster.
